facts.text: Union City was platted in 1849 by Jeremiah Smith and earned the nickname "Hub City" because five railroads converged at the state line.
Union City’s historic Union City Passenger Depot, now a landmark, is listed on the National Register of Historic Places alongside the William Kerr House and Raphael Kirshbaum Building.
A post office has operated continuously in Union City since 1852, marking the town’s long‑standing role in regional communication.
The town’s name reflects its origin as a planned community founded in 1849, sharing its name with a twin city across the Ohio border.
